title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: I is a 4-element set and G = S_I ≅ S_4. J ≅ P_{2,2}(I) is the 3-element set of partitions of I into two pairs, identified with V_I^*, the three non-trivial elements of the normal Klein subgroup V_I (the double transpositions). This page opens §4, 'Relations avec les cartes orientées'.

(1) Circ(I) is the set of the six circular permutations (4-cycles) of I. The map Circ(I) → J, u ↦ u², is G-equivariant and 2-to-1, since u and u^{-1} have the same square, a double transposition.

(2) In a bracketed NB, a second 2-to-1 equivariant map P_2(I) → J is given by A ↦ {A, ∁A}. Here P_2(I) is the set of six 2-subsets, equivalently the six transpositions ('réflexions'). In transposition language: for each reflection τ there is a unique reflection τ' with ττ' ∈ V^*.

(3) Both are 6-point homogeneous G-sets over J, but they are not isomorphic. The stabiliser of a 4-cycle is its centraliser, cyclic of order 4 (Z/4). The stabiliser of a 2-subset is S_A × S_{∁A} ≅ F_2 × F_2, a non-normal Klein group. This uses the previous page's classification of the 11 conjugacy classes of subgroups of S_4.

(4) Only the first, Circ(I), is interpreted as the set of faces of a map (carte). Via G ≅ Aut^+(cube), with I = the four main diagonals, the six faces of the cube correspond to the 4-cycles: rotations by ±90° about face axes. The marginal note says the map is compatible with the antipodism u ↦ u^{-1}, which exchanges opposite faces. The fibres of u ↦ u² are the three pairs of opposite faces, i.e. the three coordinate axes, giving J.

(5) The face poset of the cube is then described intrinsically as partial sections of the double cover Circ(I) → J:
- a face is a section over a 1-element subset of J (6 of them);
- an edge is a section over a 2-element subset of J (3·4 = 12);
- a vertex is a section over all of J (2³ = 8).
Incidence between cells of dimension 2, 1, 0 is extension of partial sections. This is the standard picture of the cube as {±}³, with the octahedron dual to it.

Purpose in the manuscript: this is the octahedral/cube map of X(4) over X(1), where PSL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4.
- The 6 cusps (stabiliser Z/4) are the faces.
- The 8 elliptic points of order 3 are the vertices, matching the 8 elements of order 3 on the next page.
- The 12 points of order 2 are the edges.
- The degree-2 map Circ(I) → J matches cusps of X(4) lying over the 3 cusps of the Legendre line X(2) with S_3 = S_4/V. The 6 cusps of X(4) lie two over each cusp of X(2), each with ramification index 2.

The next page continues with the explicit vertex, edge and face correspondences and a canonical orientation of the cube via orientation torsors.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor point: the identification of edges with sections over 2-element subsets of J is stated only sketchily ('l'ens. des 12 arêtes ... sections partielles de card. 2'). It is correct: 3 choices of the pair × 4 sections = 12.

ideas.what: Two non-isomorphic 6-point homogeneous S_4-sets (4-cycles vs 2-subsets) both mapping 2:1 equivariantly onto the 3-set J = V^*, distinguished by stabilisers Z/4 vs F_2×F_2
ideas.modern_name: Transitive G-sets classified by conjugacy classes of subgroups

ideas.what: S_4 ≅ rotation group of the cube; faces ↔ 4-cycles, opposite-face pairs ↔ double transpositions (u ↦ u²), antipodism ↔ u ↦ u^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral group; regular map {4,3} (cube) as a dessin
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps/dessins in general but not this explicit construction

ideas.what: Intrinsic description of the cube's face lattice as the poset of partial sections of the double cover Circ(I) → J (faces = sections over 1 point, edges = over 2 points, vertices = global sections), incidence = extension
ideas.modern_name: Cube as face poset of {±1}^3 / dual of cross-polytope built from a double cover

ideas.what: Implicit link to the level-4 modular curve: X(4) → X(1) as the octahedral map, with cusps = faces (stabiliser Z/4) and the degree-2 map to the cusps of X(2)
ideas.modern_name: Dessin of Γ(4); X(4) octahedral cover

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, canonical (choice-free) rendering of the classical octahedral picture of S_4 ≅ PSL_2(Z/4). It is in Grothendieck's characteristic style (constructing the cube functorially from I via partial sections of a torsor-like double cover), but the content is classical Klein material with no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'on sait maintenant des [-variétés-] de valeurs distinctes' is better read as something like 'on a maintenant deux revêtements [de degré 2] ... distincts': Circ(I) and P_2(I) as non-isomorphic homogeneous spaces under G.

'(le stabilisateur d'un n'étant pas iso[?] homogènes[?]' should read as: the homogeneous spaces are not isomorphic, since the stabiliser of an element of Circ is ≅ Z/4Z and that of a point of P_2(I) is ≅ F_2×F_2.
'des [?] d'une carte' should be 'l'ensemble des faces d'une carte' ('l'application' crossed out, replaced by 'l'ensemble').
Marginal note is approximately: 'Bien sûr la carte est compatible avec l'antipodisme u ↦ u^{-1}' (rather than 'sur la sphère').
'sous des positions de sections partielles' should read approximately 'aux ensembles de sections partielles ... & sections de card. 2 de J (resp. card. 3, sections globales) de Circ(I) sur J'.
'V ens. des faces est compl. des sommets' is approximately: V is the set of faces (replacing 'sommets'); 12 = the set of edges ('arêtes').
